title: Carpal tunnel release
what: The surgeon makes a small cut in the palm and divides the ligament that presses on the nerve. This gives the nerve more room.
why: When your fingers go numb and hurt, your hand gets weak, and injections, a splint, or other treatment have not helped.
duration: surgery usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; you usually go home the same day
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
If your other hand goes numb too
What work you do with your hands. It affects your time off

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Numbing
prepare.text: Most often the arm is numbed and you stay awake. Sometimes sedation is added. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Hand
prepare.text: Take off rings and your watch in advance. No nail polish.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: Arrange a ride home. You cannot drive after surgery.

steps: You lie down, and your arm rests on a side table
The arm is numbed with a shot
Sometimes a cuff is placed on the upper arm to reduce bleeding
The surgeon makes a small cut in the palm, or uses a camera through a small opening
The ligament is divided, and the wound is stitched
A bandage, and sometimes a splint, is applied
feel: The numbing shot burns for a few seconds
During surgery: touch and pressure, but no pain
When the numbing wears off, your palm aches. You will get pills
after: Keep your hand raised for the first days. It reduces swelling
You can and should usually move your fingers right away
Keep the bandage dry until your doctor says it is OK
Stitches usually come out after 10 to 14 days
Numbness fades gradually, over a few days to a few months
red_flags: The bandage feels very tight, or your fingers turn blue or cold
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or redness and pus from the wound
The wound bleeds heavily and does not stop with pressure

faq.q: Will the numbness go away right away?
faq.a: Night pain often goes quickly. Feeling comes back gradually, sometimes over months.

faq.q: When can I go back to work?
faq.a: Light work usually after 1 to 2 weeks, heavy work later. Your surgeon will say when.

reminders.text: Wrist surgery tomorrow. Take off your rings, bring your documents, and arrange a ride home.
